pattern_name: Future forms: will / going to / present continuous
pattern_name_ar: صيغ المستقبل: will / going to / المضارع المستمر
formula: will + verb (decision now/prediction) · be going to + verb (plan/evidence) · am/is/are + -ing (arrangement)
formula_visual: [I'll help] // [I'm going to study] // [I'm meeting Sara at 6]
when_to_use: will: instant decisions and predictions ('I'll get it', 'It'll rain'). going to: plans and predictions from evidence ('I'm going to study medicine', 'Look — it's going to rain'). Present continuous: fixed arrangements with a time/place ('I'm meeting Sara at six').
when_to_use_ar: will: قرار لحظي وتوقّع. going to: خطة وتوقّع من دليل. المضارع المستمر: ترتيب ثابت بوقت/مكان.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic marks the future mainly with سـ/سوف, so learners use 'will' for everything and rarely use 'going to' for plans or the present continuous for arrangements. They also say 'I will meeting' or 'I going to'.

examples.en: The phone's ringing — I'll get it.
Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.
I'm meeting Sara at six tonight.
I think our team will win.

common_errors.wrong: I will study medicine (a long-decided plan).
common_errors.explanation: A plan you already decided → going to, not a spur-of-the-moment will.

common_errors.wrong: I will meet Sara at six (fixed arrangement).
common_errors.explanation: Fixed arrangement with a time → present continuous.
Prediction from present evidence → going to.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: That bag looks heavy. I ___ (help) you.
I ___ (see) the doctor at 4 pm tomorrow. (arrangement)

practice_fill_blank.answer: are going to drop / 're going to drop

practice_fill_blank.sentence: I think it ___ (be) a great year.

quick_rule: Decide now/predict → will. Plan or evidence → going to. Fixed arrangement (time+place) → present continuous.
quick_rule_ar: قرار الآن/توقّع → will. خطة أو دليل → going to. ترتيب ثابت (وقت+مكان) → مضارع مستمر.
mnemonic: Just decided → 'll. Already planned → going to. In my diary → -ing.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 3 you practised gonna and 'll and time-phrase stress. Say: 'I'm gonna study medicine' and 'I'll get it' — reduce 'going to' to 'gonna' and contract 'I will' to 'I'll'.
